explain.say: Imagine everyone on Earth standing in one line. In 1800 the line would hold about 1 billion people. Today it holds more than 8 billion! Look at the board. The curve shows how the world’s population grew: slowly for a long time, then shooting up.

faq.q: How many people live on Earth?
faq.a: More than 8 billion. The United Nations marked the day the world reached 8 billion people on 15 November 2022.

faq.q: Why did the population grow so fast?
faq.a: Death rates fell sharply thanks to clean water, vaccines, medicine and more food, while birth rates stayed high for a while. With far more babies surviving, the population rose very fast.
asks: Why did the population explode in the 1900s?

faq.q: Which country has the most people?
faq.a: India, which passed China in 2023. Each has more than 1.4 billion people, and together they hold more than a third of humanity.
asks: Does India have more people than China?

faq.q: Will the world population keep growing?
faq.a: Not for ever. The UN expects it to peak at about 10.3 billion in the mid-2080s and then slowly fall, as families in most countries are getting smaller.

faq.q: Why do families have fewer children now?
faq.a: When most children survive, when girls stay longer in school and when families move to cities, people usually choose to have fewer children. Raising children in cities also costs more.

facts: The UN marked the world reaching 8 billion people on 15 November 2022.
The world reached 1 billion people around 1804 and 2 billion in 1927.
India overtook China as the most populous country in 2023, according to the UN.
